source.title_on_document: Best humans still outperform artificial intelligence in a creative divergent thinking task

supplement.where: Supplementary Information online at 10.1038/s41598-023-40858-3; data and scripts at https://osf.io/qdz3n/?view_only=d2da32d06f0f4f7ca5bd4bdfc8cf4346
supplement.holds: Supplementary Fig. 1 (distribution of the number of human ideas) and additional analyses that drop the lowest-performing humans (Discussion)

paper_design_summary: 256 native English speakers on Prolific completed the Alternate Uses Task (rope, box, pencil, candle; 30 s per object) without any AI help. Three chatbots (ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4, Copy.Ai) answered the same task in 11 sessions each, with the number of ideas and words per idea fixed to match human responses. Responses were scored for originality by semantic distance (SemDis) and by six blind human raters on a 1 to 5 creativity/originality scale, and AI scores were compared with human scores in linear mixed models.

studies.label: Alternate Uses Task: 256 humans vs three AI chatbots

participants.exclusions: 310 opened the study link; 279 gave full data; 256 passed the attention checks and were analyzed. 14 participants lack observations for some objects (unclear responses removed or no response in 30 s).
participants.who: Native English speakers recruited on Prolific, mean age 30.4 (range 19 to 40), 44 students; human data collected for another preregistered study. AI side: ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4, and Copy.Ai, 11 sessions each with four objects (33 sessions, 132 observations).
participants.quote: Of the 279 participants with full data, 256 passed the attention checks (108 females, 145 males, 2 other, and 1 preferred not to identify the gender identity) and their results were included in the present study.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT3.5 (called ChatGPT3 in the text), ChatGPT4, Copy.Ai (based on GPT-3); tested 30.3.2023 to 5.4.2023
ai_tool.how_used: The chatbots produced AUT responses themselves; no human used AI. Prompts matched the human instructions, with the number of ideas set per session (1 to 6) and responses limited to 1 to 3 words.

task.description: Alternate Uses Task with four objects (rope, box, pencil, candle); instructions stressed creative quality over quantity
task.duration: 30 s per object for humans; about 13 min for the whole human session

outcomes.name: Mean semantic distance (originality) per object
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: SemDis semantic distance between object name and response, mean of five semantic models, multiplicative composition, filler words and 'DIY'/'Make a' removed; averaged over a participant's (or AI session's) responses to each object. Mixed model with Group and Fluency fixed, random intercept per participant or session; one row per participant-object trial.

contrasts.locator: Results, Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance', Fig. 2A

outcomes.name: Max semantic distance (best response) per object
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Highest SemDis score among a participant's (or AI session's) responses to each object; same mixed model as S1-O1.

contrasts.locator: Results, Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance', Fig. 2B

outcomes.name: Mean subjective creativity/originality rating per object
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Six briefly trained raters, blind to AI involvement, rated each response 1 to 5 for creativity/originality, told to stress novelty over usefulness; averaged over responses to an object and over raters. ICCs 0.88 to 0.93 by object.

contrasts.locator: Results, Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance', Fig. 2C

outcomes.name: Max subjective creativity/originality rating per object
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Highest rated response per object, same six blind raters as S1-O3. This is the analysis revised by the 2024 Author Correction (Fig. 2D); numbers here are from the corrected text.

contrasts.locator: Results, Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance', Fig. 2D (corrected)

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: An unnamed study for which the human AUT data were originally collected; its method was preregistered at https://osf.io/fy3mn/?view_only=f1cf960d0170433dba9d31df68a6eaf7. The paper does not name that study.
sample_overlap.quote: The AUT data from human participants were collected in the context of another study and its’ method was preregistered at OSF.io in the context of that study

eligibility.reason: Only criterion 1 fails: no person was randomly assigned to generative-AI assistance; the study compares unassisted human AUT responses with chatbot-generated responses (Method, Participants and Procedure). Criteria 2 and 3 are met: 256 people were analyzed, and their output was scored for originality/creativity using SemDis and six human raters (Method, Participants and Scoring). This is AI-versus-human context evidence, so core remains no.

one_line_finding: On the Alternate Uses Task, responses from three chatbots (33 sessions) scored higher than those of 256 humans on mean semantic distance (0.95 vs 0.91) and mean rated creativity (2.91 vs 2.47; mixed model B = 0.453, SE = 0.082; Table 1; Results, 'Overall human and AI performance'), while AI did not consistently outperform the best human performers within objects (Abstract; Discussion, paragraph 4).
notes: n_units = 289 counts the 256 humans plus the 33 AI sessions in Table 1; the mixed models use one row per participant-object trial (up to 1024 human and 132 AI observations, some human cells missing). Per-chatbot contrasts (e.g. ChatGPT4 vs humans on mean rating, t(283) = -6.6649) are in Results, 'human subjective ratings', and are not listed.
